positive.prompt: Design the Rust ownership lifecycle for reserved sockets, child tasks, partial startup rollback, cancellation, and fallible cleanup
Decide how this prepared Rust service should transfer resource handles into a running state and preserve the startup error when cleanup also fails
Model an async Rust supervisor so processes and tasks cannot outlive their run and every cancellation point has a defined cleanup owner

negative.prompt: Translate this GRASP controller and strategy design into idiomatic TypeScript constructs
Specify submitOrder postconditions for created domain objects, new associations, attribute changes, and required non-creations
Coordinate this complex Rust test-environment refactoring while its system boundary, representative end-to-end oracle, module responsibilities, and parent completion boundary are still unclear
Assign preparation, coordination, supervision, and cleanup responsibilities to the right modules, functions, tasks, adapters, and composition root before exact ownership design

evals.prompt: Create an implementation-facing Rust lifecycle design for this approved validation-run system boundary, representative scenario, native responsibility map, and verification oracle. Cover preparation, ownership transfer, readiness, partial-start rollback, async cancellation, explicit completion and abort, emergency Drop behavior, and verification obligations. Prefer one existing design artifact if it already owns this lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: One traceable Rust lifecycle design realizes established system behavior and native responsibilities through explicit ownership, transitions, failure, cancellation, cleanup, and retained vertical verification without inventing product behavior or speculative abstractions.
expectations: The system boundary, representative scenario, native responsibilities, and vertical verification oracle constrain the lifecycle
Every material resource has an owner, transfer point, explicit release, and bounded Drop fallback
Preparation and the externally visible startup boundary are distinct
Partial failure and cancellation preserve the primary result while reporting cleanup failures
Traits and typestate are selected only for demonstrated variation or transition risk
Ownership evidence that changes responsibilities or verification is returned to its canonical owner
prohibitions: Do not invent business, protocol, or compatibility behavior
Do not create one class, struct, trait, or document per conceptual collaborator
